title: Low-Level Design (OOD)
scope_in: Object-oriented design interviews in C++: requirements, entities, relationships, patterns, SOLID, state machines, concurrency in design, extensibility, clean public APIs.
scope_out: Distributed architecture (prep-hld), algorithm optimisation (prep-dsa), language syntax drills.

modes.output: one LLD problem: requirements dialogue, user's design + C++ skeleton, graded vs hidden rubric with an extensibility probe
pattern/principle questions (which pattern, spot the smell, fix the violation)
problem it solves, C++ minimal example, misuse cases, relation to neighbours
revisit weak designs/smells from memory with a changed requirement
interviewer simulation: sparse prompt, clarifications on request, 1 mid-session requirement change

ladder: Tic-tac-toe, parking lot (single type), basic bank account: 3-5 classes, clear nouns/verbs.
Library system, vending machine (state), elevator (single car): one pattern needed (State/Strategy).
Splitwise, ATM, multi-elevator scheduler, chess: several patterns, invariants, validation rules.
Thread-safe LRU/cache, rate limiter, logger framework, pub-sub, task scheduler: concurrency and extensibility under change.
Plugin architecture, workflow engine, game engine core, text editor with undo/redo and collaboration hooks: layered design with strong trade-off defence.

flaws.F-MISSING-REQ: Did not clarify requirements/actors/scale before designing.
flaws.F-GOD-CLASS: One class owns too many responsibilities (SRP).
flaws.F-NO-ABSTRACTION: Concrete types everywhere; no seam for variation (OCP/DIP).
flaws.F-OVER-ENGINEERING: Patterns or layers with no requirement behind them.
flaws.F-PATTERN-MISUSE: Pattern applied to the wrong problem or implemented incorrectly.
flaws.F-TIGHT-COUPLING: Classes reach into each other's internals; hard to test or replace.
flaws.F-NO-CONCURRENCY: Shared state with no thread-safety story when the requirements imply it.
flaws.F-STATE-LEAK: Invariants can be broken from outside (public mutable state, no validation).
flaws.F-EXTENSIBILITY-FAIL: Changed-requirement probe required rewriting, not extending.
flaws.F-RESOURCE-MGMT: C++ ownership issues: raw new/delete, missing virtual destructor, copy/move mistakes.

x_fields.smells: Design smells observed in the user's design.
x_fields.extensibility_probe: The changed requirement posed and pass/fail.

items_note: prompt, hidden rubric, reference class sketch, user's last design
rubric_body:
Score each 0-2 (0 missing, 1 partial, 2 solid):

| Dimension | Looks for |
|-----------|-----------|
| Requirements | actors, use-cases, constraints, out-of-scope stated |
| Entities & relations | right nouns, ownership, cardinality |
| Responsibilities | each class one reason to change |
| Patterns & abstraction | used where variation exists, not elsewhere |
| Correctness | invariants, state transitions, error paths |
| Concurrency | shared state protected / reasoned about |
| Extensibility | handled the changed requirement without rewrite |
| Code | compiles; sensible C++ (RAII, virtual dtor, const-correctness) |
outcome_rule: Weighted total /16 (Correctness and Extensibility count double): **pass** ≥ 75% with no 0 in Correctness; **partial** 40-75%; **fail** < 40% or Correctness = 0.
gate_extra: Any C++ skeleton you show (reference or critique) must pass `g++ -std=c++20 -fsyntax-only` first; run the user's skeleton through the same check and report compile errors as `F-NOT-COMPILABLE` rather than judging by eye.
Prepare the extensibility probe (a changed requirement) at generation time, together with the hidden rubric; do not invent it after seeing the user's design.
loop_extra:
### Design specifics
Present a one-line prompt only; answer clarifying questions tersely and in character. Let the user drive; interrupt only to enforce the time box. Pose the extensibility probe after their first full design.
